provisions.text:
# Meridian Claims Regulation Part 14 (fictional)

This text is invented for the Law Machine demonstration. Meridian is not a real jurisdiction and none of these rules are real law.
Section 14.1. Scope.
(a) This Part governs written claims for money damages against an agency of the fictional Commonwealth of Meridian.
Section 14.2. When a claim is presented.
(a) A claim is presented when the responsible agency receives written notice of the incident accompanied by a claim for money damages in a sum certain.

(b) An agency that receives a claim for which it is not responsible shall transfer the claim to the responsible agency, if that agency can be identified, and shall notify the claimant of the transfer.
(c) A claim transferred under paragraph (b) is presented when the responsible agency receives it.
Section 14.3. Disposition period.
(a) If the responsible agency does not make final disposition of a presented claim within six months after it is presented, the claimant may treat the failure as a final denial.
Section 14.4. Missing amount.
(a) An agency that receives a claim that does not state a sum certain shall return the claim to the claimant with a statement that the amount is missing.
(b) A claim returned under paragraph (a) is presented when the responsible agency receives a claim that states a sum certain.

provisions.text:
# Meridian Electronic Claims and Receipt Act (fictional draft)

This text is an invented draft bill for the Law Machine demonstration. It has not been introduced or enacted anywhere, and Meridian is not a real jurisdiction.
Section 1. Short title.
(a) This Act may be cited as the Meridian Electronic Claims and Receipt Act.
Section 2. Definitions.
(a) "Intake system" means an electronic system designated by the Claims Commission to receive claims for all agencies.
(b) "Receipt time" means the time at which a submission first enters an intake system.
Section 3. Receipt.
(a) A submission is received at its receipt time, whether or not an employee has read it.
(b) The intake system shall ordinarily issue an electronic receipt within 60 seconds after the receipt time.
(c) A claim is presented when it has been received by the responsible agency and states a sum certain.
Section 4. Claims sent to the wrong agency.
(a) An agency that receives a claim for which it is not responsible shall route the claim to the responsible agency within 2 business days after the receipt time.
(b) A claim routed under subsection (a) is treated as received by the responsible agency at the receipt time of the original submission.
(c) A failure to route within the period in subsection (a) does not change the receipt time preserved by subsection (b).
(d) A claimant may file a complaint with the Claims Commission about an agency that fails to route a claim within the period in subsection (a).
Section 5. Missing amount.
(a) If a claim does not state a sum certain, the responsible agency shall notify the claimant of the omission within 15 business days after the receipt time.
(b) A claimant who supplies the missing amount within 30 days after the notice cures the omission, and the cured claim relates back to the original receipt time.
(c) The six-month disposition period begins when the claim states a sum certain.
Section 6. Disposition period.
(a) If the responsible agency does not make final disposition of a presented claim within six months after it is presented, the claimant may treat the failure as a final denial.
Section 7. System outages.
(a) When the intake system is unavailable, the Claims Commission shall provide an alternative means of submission.
(b) A submission made through an alternative means under subsection (a) is received when the alternative means accepts it.
Section 8. Effective dates.
(a) Sections 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 take effect 30 days after enactment.
(b) Section 5 takes effect 180 days after enactment.

presentment-direct.detail: Section 14.2(a) of the fictional regulation ties presentment to receipt by the responsible agency of a claim in a sum certain.

presentment-on-delivery.detail: Section 14.2(a) ties presentment to receipt by the responsible agency.

presentment-on-transfer.detail: Under § 14.2(c), the delay at the wrong agency pushes presentment later.

preserved-receipt.detail: Section 4(b) treats it as received by the responsible agency at that time.
preserved-receipt.plain: The claim keeps its original receipt time even though it went to the wrong agency.

receipt-time.detail: Section 3(a) of the fictional draft does not wait for an employee to read it.
receipt-time.plain: The claim is received the moment it enters the intake system.

return-missing-amount.detail: Section 14.4(a) states the duty but gives no deadline, so the model cannot record a late return as a breach.
return-missing-amount.plain: The agency must return a claim that has no dollar amount.

routing-complaint.detail: Section 4(d) permits a complaint. Section 4(c) says the receipt time stays the same.
routing-complaint.plain: Because the routing deadline passed, the claimant may complain to the Claims Commission.

routing-duty.detail: Section 4(a) creates a duty. Whether the agency actually meets it comes from a separate assumption.
routing-duty.plain: The wrong agency must route the claim within 2 business days.

transfer-duty.detail: Section 14.2(b) states the duty without a deadline. How fast the agency acts comes from a labeled assumption.
transfer-duty.plain: The wrong agency must pass the claim on to the right agency.
